question: Who among the following was the first Indian to win a Grammy Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ravi Shankar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar, the legendary sitar maestro, became the first Indian to win a Grammy Award, in 1967, for Best Chamber Music Performance for the album *West Meets East* (with violinist Yehudi Menuhin). (पंडित रवि शंकर — प्रथम भारतीय ग्रैमी विजेता)

 

• He later received further Grammy honours, including a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2013, and remains one of the most influential figures in popularising Indian classical music worldwide.

 

• He is often called the "Godfather of World Music" and mentored Western musicians such as George Harrison of The Beatles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian Grammy winners include A. R. Rahman (2009, for *Slumdog Millionaire*), Zakir Hussain, and Ricky Kej.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma (Option 2): A renowned santoor player who popularised the instrument in classical music, but was not the first Indian Grammy winner.

 

• Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt (Option 3): Won a Grammy in 1994 for *A Meeting by the River* (with Ry Cooder) for his invented instrument, the Mohan Veena — after Ravi Shankar's pioneering win.

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain (Option 4): The tabla virtuoso has won multiple Grammys, but after Ravi Shankar's 1967 win.

question: Chemical formula of gypsum is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaSO4.2H2O.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gypsum is a soft sulphate mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate, with the chemical formula CaSO4.2H2O. (जिप्सम — कैल्सियम सल्फेट डाइहाइड्रेट)

 

• It is widely used in the manufacture of cement, fertilizers, and Plaster of Paris.

 

• When gypsum is heated to about 150°C, it loses three-quarters of its water of crystallisation to form Plaster of Paris (CaSO4.½H2O).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's major gypsum-producing states include Rajasthan, Jammu & Kashmir, and Tamil Nadu.

 

• Gypsum is also added in small quantities to Portland cement to control its setting time.

 

NOTE

 

• CaSO4.H2O (Option 2): Represents an intermediate hydrate form, not the natural mineral gypsum.

 

• CaSO4 (Option 3): This is anhydrite, the anhydrous (water-free) form of calcium sulfate, not gypsum.

 

• CaSO4.(1/2)H2O (Option 4): This is the formula of Plaster of Paris, obtained by partially dehydrating gypsum, not gypsum itself.

question: Wangala festival is celebrated by which of the following tribes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Garo tribe.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Wangala festival, also called the "festival of hundred drums", is celebrated by the Garo tribe of Meghalaya after the harvest season, to thank the Sun god of fertility, Misi Saljong. (वांगाला महोत्सव — गारो जनजाति, मेघालय)

 

• It is celebrated over several days, typically in October-November, featuring traditional drumming, dancing, and colourful costumes.

 

• It marks the end of the agricultural cycle for the year and is one of the most important tribal festivals of Northeast India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other prominent Meghalaya festivals include Nongkrem (Khasi tribe) and Behdienkhlam (Jaintia tribe).

 

NOTE

 

• Bhil tribe (Option 1): Found mainly in Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; associated with festivals like Bhagoria.

 

• Tharu tribe (Option 3): Found along the India-Nepal Terai belt; associated with festivals like Maghi.

 

• Bhutia tribe (Option 4): Found mainly in Sikkim; associated with festivals like Losar and Losoong.

question: Which Article deals with the ‘Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 368.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 368, in Part XX of the Constitution, lays down the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure therefor. (अनुच्छेद 368 — संविधान संशोधन की शक्ति)

 

• Amendments under Article 368 require passage in each House of Parliament by a special majority (a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting), and for certain provisions affecting the federal structure, ratification by at least half of the State legislatures.

 

• In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), the Supreme Court held that Parliament's amending power under Article 368 cannot be used to alter the "basic structure" of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Constitutional amendments can be made by (i) simple majority, (ii) special majority, or (iii) special majority plus ratification by states, depending on the provision being amended.

 

• The first amendment to the Indian Constitution was made in 1951.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 352 (Option 1): Deals with the proclamation of National Emergency.

 

• Article 249 (Option 2): Empowers Parliament to legislate on a matter in the State List in the national interest, on the basis of a Rajya Sabha resolution.

 

• Article 356 (Option 4): Deals with the imposition of President's Rule in a state on failure of constitutional machinery.

question: Name the first Odissi classical dancer from Odisha who was conferred the Padma Vibhushan Award.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926-2004) was the first Odissi classical dancer from Odisha to be conferred the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award, in 2000. (केलुचरण महापात्र — ओडिसी नृत्य के पुरोधा)

 

• He is widely regarded as the chief architect of the modern revival of Odissi dance, and trained many of its leading exponents, including Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi and Protima Bedi.

 

• He had earlier received the Padma Shri in 1974, before being elevated to the Padma Vibhushan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Odissi is one of India's eight classical dance forms, originating in the temples of Odisha, particularly associated with the Jagannath Temple, Puri.

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1970.

 

NOTE

 

• Bijayini Satpathy (Option 2): A contemporary Odissi dancer and co-founder of the Nrityagram dance ensemble; has not received the Padma Vibhushan.

 

• Sonal Mansingh (Option 3): A noted Odissi and Bharatanatyam exponent who received the Padma Vibhushan in 2003, after Kelucharan Mohapatra, and is not originally from Odisha.

 

• Gangadhar Pradhan (Option 4): A respected Odissi guru and Padma Shri awardee (2005), but did not receive the Padma Vibhushan.

question: The official draw for FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup India 2022 will be held in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zurich.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The official draw for the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup India 2022 was held on 24 June 2022 at the FIFA headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland. (ज़्यूरिख — फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप 2022 का ड्रॉ)

 

• The tournament itself was held in India in October-November 2022, across venues in Bhubaneswar, Goa and Navi Mumbai.

 

• Spain won the tournament, defeating Colombia in the final; India, as hosts, featured in the tournament but did not qualify from the group stage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This was the first FIFA tournament ever hosted by India after the FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup 2017.

 

• The 2022 edition featured 16 teams divided into four groups.

 

NOTE

 

• China PR (Option 1): One of the participating teams in the tournament, not the venue of the draw.

 

• Brazil (Option 2): Also a competing nation in the tournament, not the draw location.

 

• India (Option 3): Hosted the tournament matches, but the official draw ceremony itself was held in Zurich, at FIFA's headquarters.

question: ________ is a record of assets and liabilities of any firm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Balance sheet.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A balance sheet is a financial statement that records a firm's assets, liabilities, and owners' equity at a specific point in time, reflecting its financial position. (बैलेंस शीट — संपत्ति और देनदारियों का विवरण)

 

• It follows the fundamental accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity.

 

• It is one of the three primary financial statements, alongside the income statement (profit and loss account) and the cash flow statement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A balance sheet is also known as a "statement of financial position".

 

• Assets are typically listed as current assets and fixed (non-current) assets, while liabilities are split into current and long-term liabilities.

 

NOTE

 

• Bill file (Option 1): Not a standard accounting/financial statement; not a recognised term for a record of assets and liabilities.

 

• Balance of payment (Option 2): A record of a country's economic transactions with the rest of the world, not a firm's assets and liabilities.

 

• Bank bailout (Option 4): Refers to financial assistance given to a failing bank, unrelated to a firm's assets-liabilities record.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct?

I. The Family Welfare Programme has called for promoting responsible and planned parenthood on a compulsory basis.

II. The National Population Policy 2000 provides a policy framework for providing free and compulsory education up to the age of 14 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is incorrect: India's Family Welfare Programme has always promoted responsible and planned parenthood on a voluntary basis, not a compulsory one; there is no mandatory family-planning provision in Indian policy. (परिवार कल्याण कार्यक्रम — स्वैच्छिक आधार)

 

• Statement II is correct: The National Population Policy (NPP), 2000 set several medium-term objectives, including providing a policy framework for making school education up to age 14 free and compulsory, and reducing dropout rates.

 

• The NPP 2000 also aims to achieve a stable population consistent with sustainable economic growth, social development and environmental protection.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The NPP 2000's immediate objective was to address the unmet needs for contraception, health infrastructure, and health personnel.

 

• The long-term objective of NPP 2000 is to achieve a stable population by 2045.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement II is factually correct.

 

• Only I (Option 2): Incorrect, since Statement I wrongly describes family planning as compulsory rather than voluntary.

 

• Both I and II (Option 4): Incorrect, since only Statement II is factually accurate.

question: Evangelista Torricelli is famous for which discovery?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Invention of the mercury barometer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Evangelista Torricelli, an Italian physicist and mathematician, invented the mercury barometer in 1643, providing the first method to measure atmospheric pressure. (टोरिसेली — पारा बैरोमीटर के आविष्कारक)

 

• The unit of pressure "torr" is named in his honour (1 torr ≈ 1 mm of mercury).

 

• He was a student of Galileo Galilei and succeeded him as court mathematician to the Grand Duke of Tuscany.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Standard atmospheric pressure is 760 mm of mercury (760 torr).

 

• Torricelli's experiment involved inverting a mercury-filled tube in a mercury trough, demonstrating that a vacuum ("Torricellian vacuum") forms above the mercury column.

 

NOTE

 

• Invention of the spring balance (Option 1): Commonly credited to Richard Salter, unrelated to Torricelli.

 

• Invention of the piezometer (Option 2): A device to measure pressure/compressibility of liquids, not Torricelli's key discovery.

 

• Invention of the vacuum gauge (Option 4): A general instrument for measuring pressures below atmospheric; Torricelli's specific, famous contribution was the mercury barometer.

question: Who was considered as last powerful Mughal ruler of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurangzeb.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aurangzeb (reign 1658-1707) is generally considered the last powerful Mughal emperor, under whom the Mughal Empire reached its greatest territorial extent. (औरंगज़ेब — अंतिम शक्तिशाली मुग़ल शासक)

 

• After his death in 1707, the empire went into rapid decline, weakened by prolonged wars in the Deccan, economic strain, and the rise of regional powers such as the Marathas, Sikhs, and Rajputs.

 

• His successors, often called the "Later Mughals", were largely titular rulers with little real political or military power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aurangzeb's title was "Alamgir" (Conqueror of the World).

 

• Following Aurangzeb, effective power increasingly shifted to regional and provincial powers, and eventually to the East India Company.

 

NOTE

 

• Akbar (Option 1): A powerful and celebrated Mughal ruler (r. 1556-1605), but he predates Aurangzeb; the empire remained strong for over a century after his death.

 

• Akbar II (Option 3): A titular, largely powerless Mughal emperor of the 19th century (r. 1806-1837), during British paramountcy.

 

• Shahjahan (Option 4): Aurangzeb's father (r. 1628-1658); a powerful ruler, but the empire's peak strength continued into Aurangzeb's reign.

question: Which state government has launched the CHHATA scheme to improve groundwater table in September 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The CHHATA scheme is a groundwater-recharge initiative aimed at harvesting rainwater from terraces/rooftops and channelling it to recharge the water table. (छत्ता योजना — भूजल स्तर सुधार)

 

• As per the officially released SSC CGL answer key for this question, the CHHATA scheme to improve the groundwater table was launched by the Madhya Pradesh government in September 2022.

 

• Groundwater-recharge and rainwater-harvesting schemes of this kind are typically implemented at the state/local level, often involving Public Health Engineering or Water Resources departments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2, as per the official answer key.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal), a central sector scheme, similarly aims at sustainable groundwater management through community participation in several states.

 

• World Water Day is observed on 22 March every year to raise awareness about the importance of freshwater.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Not the state credited with launching the CHHATA scheme per the official key.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Not the state credited with launching the CHHATA scheme per the official key.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): Odisha has its own groundwater and rainwater-harvesting initiatives, but is not the state marked correct for the CHHATA scheme in the official key for this question.

question: The minimum period of time taken upto which the weather variations are considered to predict the climate of a place is _______ years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Climate is defined as the average weather conditions of a place over a long period, and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) standard is a minimum of 30 years of weather data to establish a meaningful "climate normal". (जलवायु — 30 वर्ष की मानक अवधि)

 

• In contrast, weather refers to short-term atmospheric conditions (temperature, humidity, precipitation, etc.) at a given place and time, which can change from day to day.

 

• The 30-year climate normal is periodically updated by meteorological agencies (e.g., every decade) to reflect the most recent multi-decadal average.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's national weather agency, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), also uses 30-year normals (e.g., 1981-2010, 1991-2020) as reference climate baselines.

 

NOTE

 

• 20 years (Option 1): Shorter than the internationally accepted minimum period for defining climate.

 

• 25 years (Option 2): Also shorter than the standard 30-year climate-normal period.

 

• 10 years (Option 3): Considered too short a period to average out short-term weather variability and yield a reliable climate estimate.

question: The length of a Beach Volleyball court is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16 m.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Beach Volleyball court measures 16 m in length and 8 m in width, smaller than an indoor volleyball court. (बीच वॉलीबॉल कोर्ट — 16 मीटर लंबाई)

 

• It is surrounded by a free zone of at least 3 m on all sides, and the playing surface is sand, at least 40 cm deep.

 

• The net height is 2.43 m for men and 2.24 m for women, the same as in indoor volleyball.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Beach volleyball is played by teams of 2 players per side, unlike indoor volleyball's 6 players per side.

 

• Beach volleyball became an official Olympic sport in 1996 (Atlanta Games).

 

NOTE

 

• 12 m, 20 m, 15 m (Options 1, 3, 4): None match the standard, FIVB-specified 16 m court length for beach volleyball.

question: At which of the following sites was jadeite stone found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Daojali Hading.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jadeite, a hard greenish stone, has been found at the Neolithic site of Daojali Hading in the North Cachar Hills of Assam. (दाओजली हेडिंग — जेडाइट पत्थर स्थल, असम)

 

• Since jadeite is not locally available in that region, archaeologists believe it may have been brought from elsewhere, possibly further east (from areas such as China/Myanmar), pointing to long-distance trade or contact in Neolithic times.

 

• Daojali Hading is significant for its Neolithic stone tools, including hand axes and adzes, and evidence of early agriculture in Northeast India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important Neolithic sites of Northeast India include Sarutaru (Assam) and Napchik (Manipur).

 

• Daojali Hading is a Neolithic site and not itself part of the Indus/Harappan civilization, though this fact is often tested alongside questions on early material trade in the subcontinent.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahagara (Option 1): A Neolithic-Chalcolithic site in Uttar Pradesh, known for early rice cultivation and cattle-penning, not associated with jadeite.

 

• Mehrgarh (Option 2): An important early Neolithic/Chalcolithic site in Balochistan (Pakistan), regarded as a precursor to the Indus/Harappan civilization, but not the jadeite find-site.

 

• Hallur (Option 3): A Neolithic-Chalcolithic site in Karnataka, notable for early evidence of iron use, not for jadeite.

question: _______ has been elected as the 36th President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Roger Binny.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Roger Binny, a member of India's 1983 Cricket World Cup-winning team, was elected as the 36th President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) in October 2022, succeeding Sourav Ganguly. (रोजर बिन्नी — 36वें बीसीसीआई अध्यक्ष)

 

• He is the first member of the 1983 World Cup-winning squad to become BCCI President.

 

• The BCCI's other key office-bearers elected at the same time included Jay Shah as Secretary and Rajeev Shukla as Vice-President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Roger Binny was the leading wicket-taker for India in the 1983 World Cup.

 

• The BCCI is headquartered in Mumbai and governs cricket in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Ravi Kumar S, Pradeep Singh Kharola, Bhushan Akshikar (Options 1, 3, 4): None held the position of BCCI President in 2022; Roger Binny was elected to the post.

question: For pregnant women, a Special Health Care Abhiyan 'Anchal' has been launched in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rajasthan government launched a Special Health Care Abhiyan called 'Anchal' for pregnant women, aimed at reducing maternal and infant mortality through improved antenatal and health monitoring services. (आंचल अभियान — राजस्थान)

 

• The campaign focuses on providing enhanced healthcare, nutrition support, and regular check-ups for pregnant and lactating women.

 

• It forms part of Rajasthan's broader efforts to strengthen maternal and child healthcare delivery in the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan has run several maternal-health-linked schemes and campaigns to improve institutional deliveries and antenatal check-ups.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these states launched the 'Anchal' Special Health Care Abhiyan; it is a Rajasthan government initiative.

question: Which of the following are members of 15 naturally occurring metallic chemical elements whose atomic numbers are between 57 and 71?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lanthanides.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lanthanides are a series of 15 metallic elements with atomic numbers 57 (Lanthanum) to 71 (Lutetium), occurring naturally and placed together in the f-block of the periodic table. (लैंथेनाइड — परमाणु क्रमांक 57 से 71)

 

• They are also known as "rare earth elements" (along with Scandium and Yttrium), and are chemically similar due to the filling of 4f orbitals.

 

• Lanthanides are used in magnets, phosphors, catalysts, and various electronic and optical applications.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Actinides (atomic numbers 89-103) form a parallel series in the periodic table, most of which are radioactive.

 

• China holds the world's largest reserves and production of rare earth elements.

 

NOTE

 

• Alkali Metals (Option 1): Group 1 elements (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr), unrelated to atomic numbers 57-71.

 

• Halogens (Option 3): Group 17 elements (F, Cl, Br, I, At), non-metals, unrelated to this range.

 

• Actinides (Option 4): Atomic numbers 89-103, a different f-block series from the Lanthanides.

question: In the beginning of the 19th century cotton mills in India were mostly located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Modern cotton textile mills in India first developed in Bombay (present-day Mumbai), Maharashtra, which became the leading centre of the Indian cotton textile industry. (सूती वस्त्र मिलें — बॉम्बे, महाराष्ट्र)

 

• The first cotton mill in India was established in Bombay in 1854 by Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar, called the Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company.

 

• Bombay's advantages included its port location for importing machinery and exporting cloth, proximity to cotton-growing regions, and easy availability of capital and labour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ahmedabad later emerged as another major textile hub in western India, together with Bombay earning the region the nickname "Manchester of India".

 

• By the late 19th century, cotton mills had spread to other regions as well, but Bombay remained the dominant centre.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam, Punjab, Haryana (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these regions were the primary centres of India's early cotton mill industry, which was concentrated around Bombay in western India.

question: Dadabhai Naoroji offered a scathing criticism of the economic impact of British rule through his book entitled ‘__________’.
option_3: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poverty and Un-British Rule in India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji, in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (1901), offered a scathing critique of British economic policies, articulating the influential "Drain of Wealth" theory. (दादाभाई नौरोजी — निर्धनता एवं अ-ब्रिटिश शासन पुस्तक)

 

• His Drain Theory argued that a significant part of India's wealth was being systematically transferred to Britain without adequate economic return, impoverishing India.

 

• Naoroji was also the first Indian to become a member of the British House of Commons (1892) and a founding member of the Indian National Congress, later becoming its President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Naoroji is popularly known as the "Grand Old Man of India".

 

• Other early nationalist economic critiques include R.C. Dutt's "Economic History of India".

 

NOTE

 

• India Today, The Idea of India, The History of British India (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these are titles of Dadabhai Naoroji's economic critique; his actual work is "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India".

question: In March 2022, Pramod Sawant became the ____________ Chief Minister of Goa.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pramod Sawant took oath as the 13th Chief Minister of Goa on 28 March 2022, beginning his second consecutive term after the BJP's victory in the 2022 Goa Assembly elections. (प्रमोद सावंत — गोवा के 13वें मुख्यमंत्री)

 

• He had first become Chief Minister of Goa in March 2019, following the death of Manohar Parrikar.

 

• Sawant retained the top post after the BJP won a majority in the 2022 Goa Legislative Assembly elections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pramod Sawant represents the Sanquelim constituency in the Goa Legislative Assembly and belongs to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

 

• He trained as an Ayurvedic doctor before entering politics.

 

NOTE

 

• 10th, 15th, 11th (Options 1, 3, 4): These do not correspond to Pramod Sawant's position in the widely reported sequence of Goa's Chief Ministers; he is counted as the 13th.

question: Identify an option that does NOT represent prokaryotic cells.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sperm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sperm is a eukaryotic cell — it has a well-defined nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane and other membrane-bound organelles — hence it does not represent a prokaryotic cell. (शुक्राणु — यूकैरियोटिक कोशिका)

 

• Mycoplasma, blue-green algae (Cyanobacteria), and PPLO (Pleuropneumonia-Like Organisms) are all prokaryotic — they lack a defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

 

• Mycoplasma is notable for being the smallest known free-living prokaryotic organism, lacking a rigid cell wall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Blue-green algae (Cyanobacteria) are photosynthetic prokaryotes, sometimes considered a link between bacteria and true algae.

 

• Prokaryotic cells generally range from 0.1 to 5.0 μm in size, much smaller than eukaryotic cells.

 

NOTE

 

• Mycoplasma (Option 1): A genuinely prokaryotic organism, lacking a cell wall and true nucleus.

 

• Blue-green alga (Option 2): Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic, photosynthetic organisms.

 

• Pleuropneumonia-like organism (Option 4): PPLO (Mycoplasma) are prokaryotic organisms, among the smallest known cells.

question: Which of the following is NOT an aid or auxiliary to trade?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hoarding.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hoarding refers to the artificial withholding of goods from the market to create scarcity and raise prices — it is an unfair trade practice, not a recognised aid or auxiliary to trade. (जमाखोरी — व्यापार में सहायक नहीं)

 

• Aids/auxiliaries to trade are activities that facilitate the smooth flow of goods and services from producers to consumers, and include transportation, warehousing, insurance, banking, and advertising.

 

• These auxiliaries help overcome hindrances of place, time, risk, finance, and information in the process of trade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common aids to trade include communication and standardisation & grading of goods.

 

• Hoarding, by contrast, is often associated with black-marketing and is discouraged/regulated by governments through laws like the Essential Commodities Act.

 

NOTE

 

• Insurance (Option 2): A recognised aid to trade, covering the risk associated with loss of goods.

 

• Warehousing (Option 3): A recognised aid to trade, overcoming the hindrance of time/storage.

 

• Transportation (Option 4): A recognised aid to trade, overcoming the hindrance of place.

question: Who is known as the Father of Geology?
solution_text:
The correct answer is James Hutton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• James Hutton, an 18th-century Scottish geologist, is regarded as the "Father of Modern Geology" for his foundational work establishing the principle of uniformitarianism — that geological processes observed today have operated throughout Earth's history. (जेम्स हटन — आधुनिक भूविज्ञान के जनक)

 

• His seminal work, "Theory of the Earth" (1795), argued for the vast age of the Earth, shaped by slow, continuous geological processes rather than sudden catastrophic events.

 

• His ideas laid the groundwork for later geologists such as Charles Lyell, whose "Principles of Geology" popularised uniformitarian thinking.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alfred Wegener proposed the theory of Continental Drift in 1912, a key precursor to plate tectonics.

 

• Charles Lyell, another influential 19th-century geologist, is sometimes referred to as the father of modern geology in certain sources, but James Hutton is the more widely credited originator of the discipline's founding principle.

 

NOTE

 

• John Butler (Option 1): Not a recognised founding figure of geology as a discipline.

 

• Alfred Wegener (Option 2): Known for proposing Continental Drift theory, not regarded as the "Father of Geology".

 

• Art Smith (Option 4): Not a recognised founding figure of geology.

question: Mirza Kamran was the brother of which Mughal emperor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Humayun.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mirza Kamran was one of the sons of Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire, and thus the brother of Humayun, Babur's eldest son and successor. (मिर्जा कामरान — हुमायूं के भाई)

 

• Kamran repeatedly challenged Humayun's authority, governing Kabul and Kandahar, and was involved in several rebellions against him.

 

• After multiple conflicts, Humayun eventually had Kamran blinded in 1553 to neutralise the political threat he posed; Kamran later went on pilgrimage to Mecca, where he died.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Babur had four sons: Humayun, Kamran Mirza, Askari Mirza, and Hindal Mirza.

 

• Humayun's reign (1530-1540, 1555-1556) was marked by a temporary loss of the empire to Sher Shah Suri, before he reclaimed it shortly before his death.

 

NOTE

 

• Akbar (Option 2): Humayun's son, not Kamran's brother — Kamran was Akbar's uncle.

 

• Jahangir (Option 3): Akbar's son, several generations removed from Kamran, not his brother.

 

• Shah Jahan (Option 4): Jahangir's son, several generations removed from Kamran, not his brother.

question: Which of the following folk dances is primarily performed in the Indian state of Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bidesia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bidesia is a folk theatre-cum-dance form primarily associated with the state of Bihar, popularised by the folk poet-playwright Bhikhari Thakur. (बिदेसिया — बिहार की लोक नाट्य शैली)

 

• It portrays themes of migration, depicting the pain of separation experienced by wives whose husbands ("bidesi", i.e., migrants) leave their villages for work in distant cities.

 

• It blends folk songs, dance, and dialogue, and remains an important part of Bihar's folk cultural heritage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhikhari Thakur (1887-1971) is often called the "Shakespeare of Bhojpuri" for his contribution to Bhojpuri folk theatre.

 

• Other folk dance forms of Bihar include Jat-Jatin and Jhijhian.

 

NOTE

 

• Ghoomar (Option 1): A traditional folk dance of Rajasthan.

 

• Kalbeliya (Option 2): A folk dance of the Kalbeliya (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan.

 

• Kummatti (Option 4): A folk dance form of Kerala, performed during the Onam festival.
